source.title: Time Series, Vision, and Language: Exploring the Limits of Alignment in Contrastive Representation Spaces

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-modal alignment across model scales and modalities, and its results qualify convergence: alignment is induced by contrastive projection-head training, is highly uneven between modality pairs, and is weak or absent without that coupling.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on contrastively trained projection spaces and on uncoupled pretrained encoders. The paper also includes model/configuration tables and figures with many individual results; selected aggregate or comparison results are recorded below. Results cited from prior work and prompts used to generate captions are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study extends the Platonic Representation Hypothesis to time series, plots and captions. It reports how cross-modal alignment scales with frozen-encoder size and how it depends on metric, dataset, text and visual input. Its alignment is induced post hoc by contrastively trained projection heads, so its scale results show how alignable frozen encoders are, not alignment arising unaided. Its 'uncoupled' test compares raw coordinates across different models' spaces, which cannot show kernel-level convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also state that uncoupled encoders show near-orthogonal geometry, so convergence does not arise without explicit coupling. Alignment is conditional on representational format and semantic explicitness rather than uniform toward one shared representation. Scale helps but does not remove the TS–TXT gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures cosine, Procrustes, CKA, mutual kNN, and retrieval in frozen independently pretrained encoders whose outputs are mapped by trainable contrastive projection heads. It does not use the original PRH similarity-kernel scale analysis as its sole procedure, and much of the reported alignment is explicitly induced by post-hoc contrastive training.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with global versus local metric, direct versus indirect text, caption information density (with saturation at high training-time density), report language, plot visual richness, modality pairs included in the contrastive objective, encoder capacity, and projection-head optimization/training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Uncoupled pretrained time series, vision and language encoders show ~90° mean angular deviation and near-zero raw cross-modal cosine similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw embedding coordinates of independently trained models from different modalities are near-orthogonal (a basis-dependent property, distinct from kernel convergence).

fits_no_version.finding: Adding images to the contrastive objective improves TS–TXT alignment but often degrades TS–IMG alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In induced multimodal alignment, a third modality can bridge weakly aligned pairs.

record.problems: The study uses frozen backbones and trained projection heads, so its scaling results do not show spontaneous convergence during model training. Downstream capability is not measured. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for the selected findings. Some scaling evidence is figure-based and its flattened correlation labels are ambiguous. The study's own limitations note a focus on univariate series, synthetic CaTS captions, limited human-caption evaluation, domain-specific clinical text, and no end-to-end encoder fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: Selected aggregate and comparison results are recorded rather than every per-configuration entry in Appendix Tables 8–12 or every plotted point in Figures 5, 8, 10, 11, 22–24. Those detailed entries cover many individual model configurations and metrics; extracting all would exceed the 60-row cap. No row is included for cited results from other studies.

untested.parts: Convergence without an alignment objective, measured with a basis-invariant kernel or neighbourhood metric on the raw encoders; capability as distinct from parameter count.
Natural images and captions. The 'images' here are plots of time series, and alignment is learned by projection heads, not measured between independently trained models.

Not tested in the sense of the version. No mapping between two models' original representations, stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping; Procrustes is computed inside a jointly trained shared space.
Neighbour count is fixed at k = 5; no k sweep.
No experiment separating shared data from a common model of reality; plateau with scale is shown only for TS–IMG.

missing.what: Per-pair Pearson r of alignment with model size for each metric: IMG–TXT ≈0.41–0.53, TS–TXT ≈0.67–0.71, TS–IMG ≈0.09–0.28 (absolute values)
Joint encoder scaling (0.8B→5.5B→15.4B) with uneven gains, and time series encoder scaling (TimesFM 200M→500M) improving TS pairs
Human-written versus synthetic captions give only modest alignment shifts (no collapse)
Per-configuration Procrustes, CKA and mutual kNN values, with mutual kNN ~0.04–0.22; three Moirai configurations where TS–TXT exceeds TS–IMG
Batch size and temperature setting changes Procrustes from ~0.45 (b256) to >0.70 (b64)

record.verdict_notes: The key issue is method. The 'no coupling' test compares raw coordinates across different models, which cannot test PRH-style convergence, so R1/R2 are cannot_determine and the reader's V7 'challenges' label is dropped. All other alignment is induced by contrastive projection heads trained on paired data. Scale results therefore concern how alignable frozen encoders are, not spontaneous convergence. The 'images' are plots of time series, so V2 evidence is about plot–caption pairs. V4 links are removed because Procrustes is computed inside a jointly trained space. Ablations of the study's own training (R16, R17, R26–R29) are set to none.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test convergence of independently trained encoders as they naturally acquire capability, or isolate capability from parameter count. Its scale results are for frozen encoders whose representations are mapped by contrastively trained projection heads.

The study tests paired image–text representations in its trimodal contrastive setup, but does not establish a general trend for independently improving vision and language models without contrastive projection training.

The study measures paired-space fit under an optimal orthogonal Procrustes transformation and retrieval in a learned shared space. It does not test layer stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or preservation of model function after mapping.
The study compares metrics, datasets, text density, language, and visual variants, but fixes mutual kNN at k = 5 and does not test other neighbour counts.
The study discusses common data and objectives as possible explanations, but does not experimentally separate shared training data from shared objectives or a common model of reality.
